title: Serenading with Mexican singers on guitar
summary: He accompanied groups serenading sweethearts, played songs like La Guadalupana, and recalls a parody lyric.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

On the tuba? No, no. Yeah. Bass fiddle? No, that was on the guitar. On the guitar? On the guitar. Well, I'll tell you about that. You see, there was a, you know, always a system here with the high color, with the Mexicans and the Puerto Ricans. That's what you haven't got to there. Well, that vanished a long time ago. It's serenading. Mm-hmm. Say sometime about, say, 10 o'clock, maybe until 10, 12, 1 o'clock in the morning. Well, if they were going to serenade a mother or they were going to serenade a sweetheart or a wife or a friend or a friend or anything. a friend, even a friend. Naturally, they'd want to serenade them, to surprise them, and go over there and go to their door and sing. Well, some of the Mexicans that really knew how to play, well, they didn't need any compliments, they had it. But there's plenty of them that didn't do that, that's why I came in. They would come to me and say, we'd like you to be going to serenade such and such a place and we'd like you to play for us. Well, I'd just ask them what songs they were going to sing, actually, which is all Spanish, what songs they were going to sing and things like that. And they'd tell me. So I'd go with them. The senorita ever throw a roll? I'd give them the introduction and they'd start the same. They'd open up the doors and the windows and in no time they had a table spread out there with wine, food and everything you could mention. Like that. Just a serenade, you know?
